source.title: Illuminating search spaces by mapping elites
source.paraphrase: MAP-Elites organizes solutions by chosen descriptors and retains strong solutions within the resulting cells, exposing diversity and performance across the map.

research.mechanism_explanation: The paper's descriptor map motivates treating eligible rotation-feature pairs as separate scheduling cells. The callback shuffles cells reproducibly, interleaves their finite streams, removes exact JSON duplicates and drops exhausted streams. This borrows descriptor coverage, not elite replacement: the test-only context exposes no quality feedback. The independent evaluator validates opaque canonical payloads and enforces the depth-six evaluation cap.
research.hypothesis: At equal completed evaluator-call targets, interleaving eligible pair streams will produce a positive mean paired difference in unique valid cells versus synthetic_uniform_pair_selector_v1 across the selected development input/seed pairs. Synthetic quality passes are a separate descriptive outcome, with no predicted improvement.
research.falsifier: A mean paired unique-valid-cell difference of zero or less across complete development pairs would fail the coverage hypothesis. Any incomplete arm makes the target-budget comparison inconclusive and requires actual completed counts. Neither outcome establishes live performance or out-of-sample return correlation.

human_review.summary: The independent development report records complete_equal_calls in all four paired runs: each arm completed 4 of 4 evaluations. In alpha seeds 11/29 and beta seeds 11/29 order, challenger/reference cell counts were 3/3, 3/3, 3/2, and 4/2. Synthetic quality-pass counts were 2/1, 1/2, 2/2, and 1/2. These are descriptive fixture observations, not superiority evidence.
human_review.rationale: A finite round-robin queue is a small, reviewable way to spread construction attempts across descriptor cells. The mean observed paired coverage difference is +0.75 cells, while quality-pass differences are mixed (+1, -1, 0, -1). The paper motivates testing diversity but does not predict success for this callback. Proposals are not completions: the evaluator rejected one unknown payload in alpha seed 11 and one over-depth payload each in alpha seed 29 and beta seed 11. Explicit top-level depth filtering does not certify opaque payload depth; independent fixture validation prevented those rejected proposals from becoming evaluations. The callback is therefore limited to this fixture and is not a validated live graph generator. The report contains development inputs only. The held-out input remains for independent grading, and the genetic 100,000-simulation campaign remains unmeasured.
